Article history:                                         In the carbon capture and storage (CCS) process, CO2 sources and geologic reservoirs may be widely
Received 3 July 2008                                     spatially dispersed and need to be connected through a dedicated CO2 pipeline network. We introduce a
Accepted 1 September 2008                                scalable infrastructure model for CCS (simCCS) that generates a fully integrated, cost-minimizing CCS
Available online 24 December 2008
                                                         system. SimCCS determines where and how much CO2 to capture and store, and where to build and
Keywords:                                                connect pipelines of different sizes, in order to minimize the combined annualized costs of sequestering
Carbon capture and storage                               a given amount of CO2. SimCCS is able to aggregate CO2 ﬂows between sources and reservoirs into trunk
Optimization                                             pipelines that take advantage of economies of scale. Pipeline construction costs take into account
Pipeline network                                         factors including topography and social impacts. SimCCS can be used to calculate the scale of CCS
                                                         deployment (local, regional, national). SimCCS’ deployment of a realistic, capacitated pipeline network
                                                         is a major advancement for planning CCS infrastructure. We demonstrate simCCS using a set of 37 CO2
                                                         sources and 14 reservoirs for California. The results highlight the importance of systematic planning for
                                                         CCS infrastructure by examining the sensitivity of CCS infrastructure, as optimized by simCCS, to varying
                                                         CO2 targets. We ﬁnish by identifying critical future research areas for CCS infrastructure.
